Rule Content: A spool list must have a page header displayed on one single line by default.
The page header must contain program name, program title, user, run date, run time, and page number.
Page header information must be taken from SYST table only.
Layout must be: Left ? Program name, Middle ? Program title, Right ? User / Date / Hour / Page number.
For ALV reports, a simplified header layout should be used.
The default synthetic report must be composed of three parts: type of run, input indicators, and output indicators.
If the test-run flag is set, the line must be “TEST RUN EXECUTION”; otherwise it must be “REAL EXECUTION”.
For each input file, a line must display the nature of object (“FILE”), complete file name, and number of lines in the file.
One line must be created for each external object or action (output file or batch-input).
Output lines must include nature of object (“FILE” or “BI”), complete name, action description (e.g. CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE), and number of lines or number of transactions.
The error or anomaly list must be generated as a spool list and displayed after the synthetic information section.
Each error must be displayed on one single line and grouped by error message.
Each error line must start with a sequential error number followed by an error message (standard BAPI message or specific validation message).
Each error line must include the line number in the file, the first 50 characters of the erroneous line, and other significant information required for error correction.
The selection screen must display a warning message “No data selected” if the user executes the report without selecting any data.
All complex paragraphs must be documented in standard text (SO10) in English and identified in the form by standard text ID.
Standard texts must be identified and called in the program using their Standard Text ID.

Short texts that describe a block or frame of frame must not be included in standard text. the LAP chart. For CMM’s please refer to the CDS and./or CEL document and for CB’s, SIL’s, TEB’s,
